messages:
alex_k: paging — autoscaler alerts started spiking ~2387654300, GPU queue length growing rapidly on hotpath pool. Seeing 429s and sustained enqueue times > 8s. tagging oncall.
incident-bot: Incident created: P1 | gpu-capacity-surge | Affected: hosted inference (hotpath pool). Paging oncall: @tina_sre. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation
alex_k: summary logs: `pool=hotpath gpu_util=98% queue=420->950 over 12m` . Autoscaler not adding nodes — hits scale limit (max=10) and some requests are getting denied with rate policy fallback. stacktraces attached in logs channel.
maria_chen: I'm on it. First check: are any nodes in NotReady? `kubectl get nodes` looks fine. Autoscaler events show repeated "scaleAttemptFailed: quota-exceeded". Could be tiered rate policy starving token refill or handshake failing with dedicated capacity.
jamal_s: also seeing rate limiter errors upstream: `leaky_bucket: dropped=312 refill_delay_ms=12000 tier=standard->overflow`. That refill_delay looks suspiciously high.
tina_sre: taking lead. Oncall steps: 1) temporarily bump hotpath pool max to 16, 2) enable overflow to cpu-pool for non-latency-critical requests, 3) safe rollback of aggressive token refill changes from earlier config PR. Doing step 1 now.
alex_k: +1 to bump. If we can't scale, we should failover lower-priority customers to standard models to preserve SLA for enterprise tenants. Sam, can you prepare a list of top 5 impacted customers and contact templates?
sam_support: will pull the customer list and prepare message. ETA 8m. Preliminary: cust-a, cust-b high QPS tenants. Will include suggested mitigation steps and ETA for restore.
incident-bot: autoscaler: attemptedScale from 10 -> 14 returned FAILED (quotaExceeded). Provider quota shows no spare GPUs in region eu-west-1; fallback policies attempted: region-failover -> queued, but policy rate-limits cross-region failovers.
maria_chen: idea: temporarily relax cross-region failover cap to allow 2% of traffic to route to eu-central while we reprovision. That avoids having to manually request quota immediately. Any objections?
jamal_s: sounds reasonable for 15m window. Also we should revert the new ratepolicy that changed token refill math earlier today — it reduced burst tokens to 0 intentionally for misbehaving customers; combined with pool saturation it's preventing autoscaler handoff.
tina_sre: I rolled pool max to 16. Observability: queue length dropped slightly after enabling a small burst allowance, but still seeing 429s from the tiered rate limiter. I'm toggling `tier.rate.window_ms` from 120000 -> 300000 temporarily to smooth refill. Applying patch now:

```
PATCH /etc/redwood/ratepolicies/tiered.yaml
- standard: { refill_tokens: 10, window_ms: 120000 }
+ standard: { refill_tokens: 50, window_ms: 300000 }
```

jamal_s: acknowledged. After patch, watching token-meter logs. If we see < 50ms recover, we can start draining queued work to newly allowed nodes.
alex_k: customer impact check: are we seeing errors for embeddings API or just generation/chat hotpath? Logs show majority on model: gptx-hot-16. Embeddings relatively healthy.
maria_chen: correct — hotpath generation requests are the primary source. Recommend temporary model swap: route small/low-priority requests to gptx-hot-8-quant while preserving gptx-hot-16 for enterprise tokens.
sam_support: outreach draft:
"We're investigating intermittent 429s for real-time generation in EU. We're temporarily routing non-critical traffic to fallback models and expect recovery within 30-45 minutes. We'll update once autoscaling completes and token refill is stable. Apologies for disruption."
incident-bot: config-change: tier.rate.window_ms patched by t.sre (tina_sre). Change id: cfg-2387654321-4. Auto-rollback scheduled if error rate doesn't improve by +30m.
jamal_s: token-meter logs: refill rate increased, dropped requests per minute down from 420 -> 110 in 6m. Autoscaler events: now attemptScale 12 -> 16 pending; provider quota still constrained but cross-region failover started accepting some load.
tina_sre: starting gradual traffic shift: 10% -> 30% to overflow cpu-pool for small jobs. Watching latency and error budget.
alex_k: can we also temporarily ignore burst tokens for authenticated enterprise tokens so they always get served on hotpath? i.e., whitelist token prefixes for bypass. Need product/CS signoff but do it as emergency toggle.
sam_support: approved for emergency-only, sending list of enterprise prefixes now.
maria_chen: toggled whitelist. Verified in logs: enterprise requests are no longer dropped; 429s for those decreased to single digits.
incident-bot: monitoring: error_rate(generation, eu-west-1) trending down from 7.8% -> 1.2% over 14m. Queue length stable ~80. Alert status: degraded -> recovering.
alex_k: good work. Next steps: 1) file a follow-up to revert tier changes to config repo with proper load test, 2) long term: increase provider quota or multi-region prewarm for peak windows, 3) revisit token refill algorithm to avoid zero-burst policies during pool saturation.
tina_sre: I'll post a short postmortem draft once we confirm full recovery. For now I'll keep the pool max at 16 for 30m and then step down to normal if stable.
sam_support: customer messages sent to top 5. Two customers acknowledged and asked for postmortem.
jamal_s: note for postmortem: root cause appears to be combined effect of provider quota exhaustion + aggressive ratepolicy change earlier today reducing burst tokens to near-zero. Autoscaler couldn't fully hand off because of cross-region cap and token refill starvation.
alex_k: agreed. Marking incident as mitigated for paging purposes. Keep thread open for postmortem edits. :thumbsup:
